neighbours.label: the comma or ' I' that opens a speaker's hedging aside inside a parenthesis ('(the lathe, I believe)', '(or by machine, if you are in a hurry)')
fire: Her first novel (the short one, I believe) was reprinted twice last year.
You can dry the herbs in the oven (or in the sun, if you have the patience) before storing them.
One of the founders (the chemist, I think) later moved to Geneva.
The path is easy to follow on foot (or by bike, if you like hills) all the way to the lake.
The second engine (a diesel, I believe) was fitted after the war.
Guests may pay at the desk (or by card, if they prefer) on the day of arrival.
The oldest of the bells (the tenor, I am told) cracked in a hard frost.
Notes can be kept in a ledger (or on a napkin, if you want to be casual) during the tasting.
quiet: Her first novel (the short one about Lisbon) was reprinted twice last year.
You can dry the herbs in the oven, hang them in the shed and store them in jars.
One of the founders (a chemist from Basel) later moved to Geneva.
The path is easy to follow on foot, and it runs all the way to the lake.
The second engine (a diesel built in Leeds) was fitted after the war.
I believe the guests may pay at the desk on the day of arrival.
The oldest of the bells, the tenor, cracked in a hard frost.
Notes were kept in a ledger (bound in green cloth) during the tasting.

notes: Card: peaks on ',' and ' I' where a parenthetical turns into the writer's own comment. Probes: 0.66 and 0.53 on two such asides, but only 0.08 on '(on a Tuesday, I think)', so the trigger is not fully pinned down. Near misses keep the parentheses or the comma and drop the aside.
